messages:
Maya: quick question — when creating an A/B in Console should we let users set per-variant QPS/RPS caps in addition to % split? Some Dedicated customers want hard throughput guarantees for a variant.
Jon: +1 for exposing caps. Percentage-only feels too fuzzy for capacity planning. But need to decide precedence: do caps override % or vice versa?
Sanjay: caps should be a guard, not the primary assignment. Reason: percent routing is what users expect for experiments; caps should prevent overload. So: percent -> compute desired qps -> clamp by variant cap.
Ellie: UX note: if we show both, we need clear language and a preview of resulting traffic (e.g., estimated requests/sec per variant given current traffic). Otherwise people will be surprised.
Maya: agreed. Also need ramp controls: max % increase per minute to avoid instant blast when turning on a variant.
Jon: for API, we can add fields to the experiment create payload: `max_qps_per_variant` and `ramp_rate_pct_per_min`. Example: 
```json
{
  "name": "homepage-personalization",
  "variants": [
    {"key":"control","pct":90},
    {"key":"treatment","pct":10, "max_qps": 50}
  ],
  "ramp_rate_pct_per_min": 20
}
```
Sanjay: that shape works. Backend needs to translate `pct` + current_global_qps -> target qps and apply `max_qps` clamp. Also need a fallback policy when capacity is exhausted (route to control or degraded model).
DeployBot: deploy started: rollout-service v2.3 -> will add new experiment schema validation.
Nate: telemetry: make sure we tag requests with `experiment_id`, `variant_key`, and `routing_decision` (e.g., pct, cap, fallback). We'll need those to compute true exposure and to debug when caps kick in.
Lisa: SRE concern: adding `variant_key` as a label will increase metric cardinality. Suggest we map variant_key to a short hashed id label to keep Prometheus cardinality down. Also aggregate exposures by experiment_id -> variant_hash.
Ellie: Console UX mock: show a line in the create flow "Estimated traffic per minute" with current baseline traffic pulled from route metrics and a small chart of projection over ramp steps. Include a toggle "Enforce hard QPS caps (might change % distribution)" with tooltip.
Maya: question on validation: should we block creating an experiment where sum(pct)>100 or where `max_qps` sum < minimum reserve? We should validate pct sum==100 and warn if caps make effective pct differ >5% from requested.
Jon: server-side: require `pct_total==100` unless `serve_unassigned` is explicit. For caps we return a 202 with `effective_distribution` in response so UI can render exact mapping.
Sanjay: routing engine needs two small changes: 1) accept a per-variant `hard_cap_qps` and expose an rpc to the router to check remaining headroom. 2) add a deterministic fallback mapping when a request can't be admitted (route to control/tier-fallback).
Maya: also add audit log entry when fallback happens with reason code `CAP_EXCEEDED`.
Nate: telemetry items: exposures, fallback_count, cap_hits, and per-variant latency. Tie into existing per-route SLO dashboards.
Lisa: ops playbook: if cap_hits > 1% for >5m, alert to infra and product; include `experiment_id` and `variant_hash` in pager payload.
Ellie: small UI ask: when creating variant allow an optional description field that surfaces in logs and telemetry (but truncate it before sending to metrics to avoid PII).
Jon: action list: I'll sketch the API PR with schema + `effective_distribution` field. Maya, can you do a small Console mock showing the preview and toggle? Nate, can you outline the telemetry labels + alert thresholds? Sanjay, can you adjust routing rpc to accept headroom checks?
Maya: yep I'll do mock, will attach PNG in this thread when ready.
Sanjay: starting on router changes, will open draft PR and link here.
Nate: will post telemetry plan tomorrow, will call out retention/cost tradeoffs.
Jon: thanks. I'll open an RFC doc for the precedence rules (pct vs caps vs fallback).
Maya: cool. pinging @Ellie for UX review once mock up. :thumbsup:
DeployBot: deploy completed: rollout-service v2.3 -> schema validation enabled.
